title: Pan-STARRS1 timing from 2010-2014 rejects a constant period decrease in the 56-minute binary ZTF J2055+4651; a 15-41 year third-body orbit or a period change near 2021 fits the 2010-2025 data
abstract: Question: ZTF data from 2018 to 2025 show that the orbital phase of the 56-minute mass-transferring sdOB + white dwarf binary ZTF J2055+4651 drifts by about 300 s. A quadratic gives Pdot = -3.4e-11, 26 times the gravitational-wave value. Is this a constant period decrease? Method: We timed 80 Pan-STARRS1 DR2 detections from 2009-2014 and five TESS full-frame-image sectors from 2022-2024 with the ZTF light-curve templates, on the same ephemeris and zero point. We then fitted the O-C values of ZTF, PS1 and TESS together with a line, quadratic, cubic, a light-travel-time (LTT) orbit and an abrupt period change. Results: PS1 gives O-C = +199 +- 10 s in 2012, and +226 and +180 s for its two halves. The constant Pdot fitted to ZTF predicts -121 and +11 s (chi2 = 62 for 2 points). With a free PS1 offset, the PS1 slope alone rejects it at 6.6 sigma. Four template choices, a quality cut and timing of the ellipsoidal harmonic alone give +195 to +233 s. TESS confirms the ZTF drift independently (-114 +- 7 s from 2022.7 to 2024.7). In joint fits, a constant Pdot fails (chi2 = 91.6 for 26 dof). An LTT orbit fits (chi2 = 26.5 for 24 dof): outer period 19 yr (14.8-41 yr at delta chi2 < 4), amplitude 97 s, minimum third-body mass 0.030 solar masses. A period change near 2021 also fits (delta BIC = 5 against the LTT orbit). The period was nearly constant from 2010 to 2019. Limitations: the pre-ZTF test uses one survey with a reduced chi2 of 6-11 against the templates; models other than constant Pdot are not strongly separated; a third body is not confirmed.

display.caption: O-C of ZTF J2055+4651 from Pan-STARRS1 (2010-2014), ZTF (2018-2025) and TESS (2022-2024), with the constant-Pdot extrapolation from ZTF (red dashed), the joint third-body LTT fit (violet, 16-84% band), a cubic and an abrupt period change. Lower panel: residuals from the LTT fit.

Left: PS1 shift scans for three template choices; the constant-Pdot prediction is far from the minimum. Middle and right: PS1 g and r fluxes folded on the reference ephemeris, with the ZTF template at the best PS1 shift and at the constant-Pdot prediction.
Timing from the ellipsoidal (second) harmonic alone gives the same PS1 offset as the full template, so a disc-eclipse shape change does not cause it.

citations.reason: We reuse its ZTF data recipe and timing code, reproduce its J2055 O-C, and test its open question with PS1 and TESS; our joint LTT solution agrees with its 18-yr alternative and our data reject the constant-Pdot reading of its quadratic.
